summary: Jan Dolensky specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna, completing his Magister der Philosophie in 2013 under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan Gonda was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (PhD 1929) and at Leiden University. He was a professor at Utrecht University (1932–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago.
Jan Jaworski worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1922–1927) under Stanisław Schayer and later studied under Jean Przyluski (~1928–1930).
Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1908–1913). He later held an academic post at Leiden University from 1919 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer works in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (~1962–1969) and the University of Bristol (~1968–1970), later holding posts at Utrecht University (~1978–1990) and the University of Groningen (~1990–2009).

Jan Nattier specializes in Buddhist studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Sinology. She studied at Indiana University and Harvard (PhD 1988 under Masatoshi Nagatomi), later holding professorships at Hawaii, Stanford, Macalester, Indiana, Soka, Berkeley, and the University of Tokyo.

Jan P. Hogendijk works in history/archaeology and Indology. After studying at Utrecht University (~1974–1983), he held posts at Utrecht, Brown, Goethe University Frankfurt, Leiden (~2004–2009), Heidelberg, the University of Tehran, and King Fahd University.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2006) under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper, alongside training under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Westerhoff specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Cambridge and SOAS, later serving as Lecturer in Philosophy at Durham University (~2009–2012) and University Lecturer in Religious Ethics at the University of Oxford (~2013).

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1949). He held the chair of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies at Leiden (1956–1965) before becoming Head of Department at the Australian National University (1965).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under David P. Jackson (~1993–2000) and held posts at the University of Hamburg (~1995–2003), University of Copenhagen (2003–2006), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2003–2007).
Jane Bunnag is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of London (~1965–1969) under the supervision of E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (~1981). She taught at Stony Brook and Amherst College before becoming Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University (~2001–2002).

Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley (~1974–1985) under Delmer M. Brown, later holding academic posts at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu (~1993–2004).

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Chun's studies included doctoral work under supervisor Minoru Kiyota (~1988–1993), as well as instruction from Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell and Columbia University (PhD ~1976 under Alex Wayman) and served as a professor at Wesleyan University (~1977–2014).

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Ronis earned a PhD at the University of Virginia (~2002–2011), with committee members including David Germano, Nicolas Sihlé, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Clarke Hudson, and later held a post there.

Jared Rhoton specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed dissertation studies at Columbia University (~1975–1985) under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman and studied under Sakya Trizin and traditional teacher Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (PhD 1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn. He served as Assistant Professor at Uppsala University from 1908 to 1935.

Jason Birch is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (~2007–2013) under Alexis Sanderson and held posts at the University of Oxford and SOAS University of London (~2015–2020).
